status: authored 2026-10-05; written by tools/bank.py into modpack/config/cobbledollars/bank.json (installed by tools/reapply.py install, live on `cobbledollars reload` or a boot); NOT run in game (experiment below), NOT independently audited (audit_checklist)
owner_brief: the owner, 2026-10-05, during the play test: 'need to make a way for players to earn money playing through minecraft game loop, like selling minerals in brocks town or something.'

mechanism.summary: CobbleDollars' own Bank. Every CobbleDollars merchant (cobbledollars:cobble_merchant: every stall keeper in data/markets.json, Hollin's apricorn stall, the BCA shopkeepers of data/traders.json) opens it on shift + right-click, or from the Bank button on its shop screen. The player puts items in and presses Sell; each stack is paid at the bank's unit price times its count. The price list is ONE server-wide file, config/cobbledollars/bank.json: no per-merchant, per-town or per-player list exists in the installed version. So the buyer in Brock's town is every merchant on Stoneford's square, and the same buyer stands in every town that has a merchant; tiering is by WHAT is sold (deep ores and rarer drops pay more), not by where.
mechanism.rung: configuration (CLAUDE.md principle 6): a mod's documented config file, no datapack, no function, no NPC. The cheaper rung (Cobblemon native) has no sell-back; the next one (an addon already installed: CobbleDollars) has it, and its list is a config file
mechanism.why_not_a_dialogue_buyer: a dialogue NPC that takes N items with `clear` and pays with `cobbledollars give` would be the functions rung. It would buy per town at per-town prices, but it adds a purchase function per item, a menu per town and a double-submit guard, to do what the bank already does for every item at every merchant. Nothing in the owner's ask needs a per-town price; nothing here is a written failure of the bank. Kept as the fallback if the experiment below fails
verified: CobbleDollars-fabric-2.0.0+Beta-5.1+1.21.1.jar (the server's installed copy, the jar file only), read 2026-10-05 with python zipfile and javap:

fr.harmex.cobbledollars.common.network.handlers.server.SellHandler.handle: requires the player's open menu to be a BankMenu, takes SimpleContainerExtensionsKt.getBankableItems(menu.getBankContainer()), and for each stack adds CobbleDollars.INSTANCE.getBankConfig().getBank().get(stack).getPrice() x count to PlayerExtensionKt.getCobbleDollars(player), then setCobbleDollars. No merchant, town or player key is read: the list is global

the same handler never reads CommonConfig: cobbleDollarsIncomeMultiplier is read only in fr.harmex.cobbledollars.common.event.CobbleDollarsEventsKt (battle victories, NPC and wild). So the bank is NOT scaled by our 1.25 multiplier (answers docs/mechanics/PROGRESSION_LADDER.md U-1 statically; not run in game)

fr.harmex.cobbledollars.common.world.item.trading.shop.Bank extends ArrayList<Offer> with get(ItemStack); the match is MiscUtilsKt.isSame, which compares the item AND its data components (method_57353), so a renamed or otherwise changed stack does not sell

fr.harmex.cobbledollars.common.config.BankConfig: PATH = "config/cobbledollars/bank.json"; the only field is `bank` (BankAdapter reads the key `bank`, an array of the shape base-pack/cobbleverse/config/cobbledollars/bank.json carries: {item, price})

fr.harmex.cobbledollars.common.world.entity.CobbleMerchant.mobInteract (method_5992): player.isShiftKeyDown (method_5715) -> PlayerExtensionKt.openBank, else openShop. The entity's only own NBT key is CobbleMerchantShop: there is no per-merchant bank field

fr.harmex.cobbledollars.common.client.gui.screen.ShopScreen builds a BankButton that sends OpenBankPacket(merchant UUID); OpenBankHandler opens the bank for any entity that is a CobbleDollarsShopHolder

fr.harmex.cobbledollars.common.command.CobbleDollarsCommand: literals cobbledollars (alias cd), give, remove, set, query, pay, leaderboard, reload. `reload` calls BankConfig.Companion.load, CommonConfig.Companion.load and ShopConfig.Companion.load and sends SyncShopConfigPacket(defaultShop, bank) to players: a new bank.json takes effect without a restart
mechanism.what_else_pays: battle victories, by CobbleDollarsEventsKt (earnCobbleDollarsFromNPC and earnCobbleDollarsFromWildPokemon both true in modpack/config/cobbledollars/common.json, scaled by cobbleDollarsIncomeMultiplier 1.25); RCT trainers pay through that same NPC path (docs/research/INCOME_MEASUREMENT.md, relayed). Nothing else in the installed set was found paying dollars: the authored machinery only ever charges (`cobbledollars remove` in markets, ferries, blackout)

rules: the output is the base file's entries in their order, unchanged, followed by `buys` in their order: CobbleDollars reads one file, so ours must carry the base's list too (tools/markets.py bank_prices reads base then ours and agrees with this)
a `buys` item already in the base is refused: changing a base price is a separate, named decision
every price is a positive whole number (the file's own shape; Offer.price is a BigInteger)

no item is bought that any authored shop sells at or below the bank's price: buy-low-sell-high is free money (tools/markets.py's own rule, applied here to every sell point the tool can read; see tools/bank.py for the list and what it does not cover)

never_buy holds: the evolution stones (the faces restore every 600 s and the Exchange never buys, data/traders.json stock_policy.stones), every block a spawn condition names (data/spawn_blocks.json: paying for one pays players to strip encounters out of the world), and the storage blocks that craft back into a bought item
a bought item whose id is a spawn-condition block is allowed only when `in_place` is true: the item comes from harvesting a block that stays where it is (in_place_evidence)
a smelted item pays at least its raw ore and at most raw + 2: smelting is worth a little, never a lot (a furnace and fuel are the cost)
every town in buyer_towns has at least one sited CobbleDollars merchant (a data/markets.json stall), so the bank opens there
in_place_evidence: an apricorn's and a berry's item id is also its block's, and data/spawn_blocks.json names those blocks (Pineco, Morpeko and others need them near). Selling the fruit does not take the block out of the world: Cobblemon-fabric-1.8.0+1.21.1.jar, ApricornBlock.harvest drops the fruit (method_9497) and sets AGE to 0 on the same block (method_8652), so the fruit regrows where it hung; BerryBlock.harvestBerry pops BerryBlockEntity.harvest's berries and sets no block (read with javap 2026-10-05). Breaking the block by hand still removes it; that is true with or without a price

The critical-path towns are all listed (a player passes through each); the mining town (Fossick) because it is where a miner goes

income_estimate.label: ESTIMATE, not measured. Rates are ASSUMED vanilla-like ore density for WorldPainter's Resources layer (docs/world-building/REEXPORT.md: 'vanilla ores everywhere'), one player mining continuously without Fortune; nobody has timed it in this world
income_estimate.early_hour: stone pickaxe, caves above y0, the first two hours: coal 60 x $4 + raw iron 30 x $8 + raw copper 40 x $2 + lapis 15 x $4 = $620 an hour
income_estimate.deep_hour: iron pickaxe, deep caves: the early hour plus raw gold 10 x $20 + redstone 25 x $2 + diamond 4 x $120 = $1,350 an hour
income_estimate.apricorn_farm: the farm's 550 fruit (data/apricorn_farm.json decisions_pending, measured by its plan) at $1, a full grove harvest every ~17 minutes at best: Cobblemon 1.8.0 ApricornBlock.randomTick grows one stage on nextInt(5) (read from the jar 2026-10-05), so three stages take ~15 random ticks, ~17 minutes at the default randomTickSpeed 3 (ASSUMED unchanged). A player who does nothing else picks perhaps 1,000-1,500 an hour: $1,000-1,500 an hour, shared by everyone at the farm
income_estimate.against_the_ladder: battle income to badge 1 is $9,475 (data/markets.json income_basis, model B, relayed). If leg 1 takes about three hours (ASSUMED), battles pay about $3,150 an hour, so mining pays a fifth to two fifths of fighting. A player who mines for one hour on the way to Brock adds $620-1,350: the Mart basics ($1,600 a leg, PROGRESSION_LADDER 0.3) or one counter line, not the shelf. Stoneford's critical ask is $6,000 of the counter plus $7,500 for the crafting upgrade; buying that upgrade by mining alone is 6-12 hours, by picking apricorns 5-7
income_estimate.what_it_does_not_buy: the curve (tools/markets.py curve) is NOT changed: it still prices against battle income alone. Gathering is the margin a player who digs earns, not a term the shelves were priced on
